observed_original_abi.calling_convention_rationale: The body at 0x00b3d230 is two instructions and six bytes: 0x00b3d230 A1 C0 EA 67 01 (MOV EAX, DS:0x0167eac0) and 0x00b3d235 C3 (bare RET, no immediate). It reads no register, so no register can carry a receiver; it names no memory operand on ESP or any stack displacement, so it reads no stack argument; and the terminal RET carries no immediate, so the callee pops zero bytes. With zero parameters, zero receiver and a bare RET, the encoding is byte-identical under __cdecl, __stdcall, __thiscall and __fastcall -- the four differ only in where a receiver or arguments arrive and how much the callee pops, and this body has neither. The two discriminator-bearing conventions (__stdcall's callee pop, __fastcall's ECX/EDX receiver pair) are both excluded by construction, and __cdecl vs __thiscall then differ only in a receiver that 0x00b3d230 never consumes. The machine-derived ABI record for this target agrees and abstains: conventions.calling_convention null, confidence UNKNOWN, abstained_because 'no_discriminator: no stack-argument read and no positive receiver evidence'. No convention is asserted here; null is the machine's answer, not a gap.
observed_original_abi.receiver_rationale: 0x00b3d230 is A1 C0 EA 67 01, an accumulator load with a four-byte absolute operand, and 0x00b3d235 is C3. There is no register read anywhere in the six bytes, so ECX -- the only register __thiscall could deliver a receiver in -- is never consumed. The machine-derived receiver record says present: false, register: null, offsets: [], confidence OBSERVED. No field offset is claimed because no object is addressed: the single memory operand is an absolute address, not a base-plus-displacement.
observed_original_abi.return_type_rationale: 0x00b3d230 MOV EAX, DS:0x0167eac0 writes the whole 32-bit accumulator, so the value returned is a four-byte word and the width is fixed. The body proves a four-byte LOAD and nothing about what the word denotes: it contains no dereference, no arithmetic and no type test. The machine-derived record classifies the value pointer_like (inference RT2, INFERRED), and two callers null-test it (0x00c0d3c0 TEST EAX,EAX / JE, and 0x00c38532 the same), which is consistent with that classification -- but a caller's null test is a use, not a type, and the body settles nothing. No pointer type is asserted and the word is returned as an opaque uint32.
observed_original_abi.return_semantics: the four bytes stored at absolute address 0x0167eac0, whole, in EAX
observed_original_abi.ret_form_rationale: 0x00b3d235 is the single byte C3, the bare near return with no immediate operand. There is no 0x04/0x08/0x0c immediate, so the callee pops nothing.
observed_original_abi.termination: RET at 0x00b3d235 (bare C3, no immediate operand); the instruction after it, 0x00b3d236, is a CC int3 pad byte, so the function has exactly one exit and it is the terminal RET
observed_original_abi.stack_cleanup_rationale: 0x00b3d235 is a bare C3 with no immediate, so the callee pops nothing, and the body pushes nothing and reads no stack word, so there is nothing for the caller to reclaim either. With zero stack words on the call, cleanup is a no-op under either side and the owner is not distinguishable; 'none' records that no side performs cleanup. (The machine-derived cleanup record labels the side 'caller' with bytes 0 at INFERRED confidence, which is the same zero-byte fact read from the caller side; it is not a second source of information and does not contradict the zero.)
observed_original_abi.stack_frame: none; no EBP frame is established, no PUSH or POP appears, and no memory operand names ESP
observed_original_abi.flags: none; neither instruction reads or writes EFLAGS, and neither is a flag test

Who writes 0x0167eac0. This body never stores to it and no writer was identified in this session; the 60 callers of this VA are all readers. Until a writer is found the dword's lifecycle is unknown.

Which calling convention the original compiler used. Zero parameters, no receiver and a bare RET make the four x86-32 conventions byte-identical here, and 60 direct call sites that push nothing narrow the field to 'no arguments passed' without selecting a convention.

Whether the 60 callers share a common owner or a common subsystem role. The index record labels the VA subsystem Simulator, but that is a triage label and no caller was reconstructed here to corroborate it.

notes: Reconstructed from the two-instruction, six-byte body at 0x00b3d230 and its raw bytes, re-read for this sidecar rather than taken from the briefing. The reconstruction is total for this body: the single MOV and the single RET account for all six bytes, the one memory read, the one register write, the one exit. Three things are deliberately left unclaimed. The calling convention is null because the body cannot discriminate it -- no register read, no stack operand, a bare RET, which is byte-identical under all four x86-32 conventions -- and the machine-derived ABI record abstains for exactly that reason. No pointer type is asserted for the four-byte return, because a load is not a type and a caller's null test is a use, not evidence of one. No class, vtable or field offset is claimed, because the xref export shows no DATA reference to this VA at all. The one substantive fact about the target is the single dword read at 0x0167eac0, and it is carried with the exact sidecar row as its evidence. subsystem and cluster are copied verbatim from the index record and are triage labels; no semantic claim in this record rests on them.
